## What to check, in order

**1. Turn on CloudWatch Transaction Search (once per account and Region)**
- AgentCore only emits spans for viewing after this is on. Without it you get logs and metrics but no connected traces.
- In the console, go to CloudWatch > Application Signals > Transaction search, choose **Enable Transaction Search**, and tick **ingest spans as structured logs**.
- Via API or CLI, do these three steps:
  - Add a CloudWatch Logs resource policy that lets `xray.amazonaws.com` write to `aws/spans` and `/aws/application-signals/data`.
  - Run `aws xray update-trace-segment-destination --destination CloudWatchLogs`.
  - Optionally set the sampling percentage with `update-indexing-rule`.
- If you deploy with the AgentCore CLI, `agentcore deploy` does this for you unless you opted out.

**2. Instrument the agent code with ADOT**
- Service-level spans such as `AgentCore.Runtime.Invoke` come for free. The inner steps (LLM calls, tool calls, framework spans) need the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry in your agent.
- Add `aws-opentelemetry-distro` (version 0.18.0 or later) to your dependencies and start the app with `opentelemetry-instrument`.
- If it isn't instrumented, you get the outer invoke span and nothing inside it. That looks like isolated entries.

**3. Check where the spans go**
- Newer agents in supported Regions send spans to the `spans` stream of `/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/<agent_id>-<endpoint>`. Older agents send them to the shared `aws/spans` log group.
- Look in the right place for your agent.
- You can switch an existing agent with the `UNIFIED_TRACES_DESTINATION_ENABLED` environment variable. That needs ADOT 0.18.0 or later and `logs:PutResourcePolicy` on the execution role.
- Changing the destination doesn't move spans that were already delivered.

**4. Turn on tracing for Gateway, Memory and the built-in tools**
- Service-provided spans for these are configured per resource. Memory needs tracing enabled when you create it. Gateway, Browser and Code Interpreter need trace delivery to CloudWatch.
- If tool calls through Gateway don't show up as child spans, this is the likely cause.

**5. Pass trace context and a session ID across every hop**
- Send `X-Amzn-Trace-Id` or the W3C `traceparent` header on every call into and out of the agent. Include calls through SQS, EventBridge and your own APIs.
- Send the same runtime session ID on each request. This lets you group multi-turn conversations.
- If the agent runs outside AgentCore, such as on Lambda, ECS or EKS, instrument it with ADOT and set the OTEL environment variables. Those variables export to CloudWatch with your log group and service name. The "agents hosted outside of AgentCore" section of the observability guide lists the exact values.
- Put `trace_id`, `session_id` and `agent_id` in your structured logs so log lines can be matched to traces.

- The CloudWatch Generative AI Observability dashboard and the AgentCore observability page show the connected view.
